key_insight: Boron nitride nanotubes host multiple room-temperature single-photon emitters at different visible wavelengths within a compact, approximately 25 nm radius.
engineering_relevance: These nanotubes offer a potential platform for compact multiwavelength quantum light sources integrated with waveguides and interferometric filters.
method: Locate and characterize emitters using confocal photoluminescence microscopy.
Assess single-photon emission using Hanbury Brown–Twiss interferometry.
Apply surface passivation or coating to reduce blinking.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports emitters spanning the visible spectrum, multiple emission wavelengths along individual tubes, lifetimes as short as 0.5 ns, and improved stability after surface treatment.
watch_item: Deterministic placement and photonic-circuit integration remain prospective; the abstract provides no quantitative photon-purity or long-term stability metrics.
paper_title: Room-Temperature Quantum Emission from Boron Nitride Nanotubes
